title: Nobody can log in
summary: At 06:00 UTC the TLS certificate used by auth-service expired (notAfter 2026-10-09T06:00:00Z). Both edge-gateway (client) and auth-service (server) immediately logged TLS‑handshake failures, causing a spike in edge‑gateway error_rate from 0.2 % to >11 % and 5xx on all POST /v1/session requests. The only production change in the preceding hour was an unrelated keep‑alive‑timeout increase on edge-gateway (chg:2541). No certificate‑rotation change was recorded. The root cause is a missed certificate rotation for auth-service.

hypothesis.mechanism: The auth-service server TLS certificate expired at 06:00Z. Clients (edge-gateway) attempting TLS handshakes receive an expired certificate, causing handshake failures logged on both sides. Failed handshakes translate to 5xx responses for session routes.
predictions: Renewing the auth-service certificate and reloading the service will eliminate TLS handshake errors and restore error_rate to baseline.
No other services that do not call auth-service will be affected.

hypothesis.mechanism: Increasing the upstream keepalive timeout altered connection pooling in a way that caused TLS validation to fail.
predictions: Reverting the keepalive timeout would immediately stop TLS errors.

hypothesis.mechanism: A recent (unrecorded) code change in auth-service introduced a bug that rejects valid client certificates, logging 'bad certificate'.
predictions: Rolling back the auth-service deploy would stop the errors.

hypothesis.mechanism: An infrastructure‑level CA or certificate store expired, affecting both gateway and auth-service.
predictions: Other services using the same CA would show similar TLS failures.

facts.statement: edge-gateway logged 1,428 TLS handshake failures with message 'certificate has expired or is not yet valid (notAfter 2026-10-09T06:00:00Z)' starting at 06:00:09.657Z.
auth-service logged 1,112 TLS handshake errors 'remote error: tls: bad certificate' starting at 06:00:06.184Z.
The only change in the 05:00‑07:00 window for edge-gateway or auth-service was a config change on edge-gateway at 05:52:30Z raising upstream.keepalive_timeout_s from 60 to 75 (chg:2541).
edge-gateway error_rate metric rose from a baseline of 0.0021 to 0.1166 (≈55×) by 06:30Z.
edge-gateway rps, latency_p50, latency_p99, cpu_util, and mem_util remained within normal ranges throughout the window.

assumptions.statement: The notAfter timestamp in the TLS error messages reflects the actual expiry of the auth-service server certificate.
assumptions.reason: Both client and server logs cite the same notAfter value; no other component changed at that moment.

assumptions.statement: No other component (gateway trust store, CA, load‑balancer) changed its certificate configuration at 06:00Z.
assumptions.reason: Change history shows only the unrelated keepalive timeout change; no secret_rotation or config_change for certificates.

assumptions.statement: Changing the keepalive timeout cannot cause TLS certificate validation failures.
assumptions.reason: Timeout changes affect connection reuse, not certificate verification logic.

assumptions.statement: A code regression in auth-service would not produce the exact 'certificate has expired' message.
assumptions.reason: That message originates from the TLS library when validating the peer's certificate.

assumptions.statement: A shared CA expiry would show the same notAfter on both client and server logs, which is not observed.
assumptions.reason: Only the server certificate's notAfter appears in the gateway logs.

gaps.reason: No secret_rotation change record found for auth-service before 06:00Z; expected a chg: entry for certificate renewal.

gaps.scope: AZ‑b log shards for edge-gateway and auth-service
gaps.reason: Log shard for az-b was unavailable, potentially hiding early warnings or a partial rollout.
No auth-service metrics were queried; would help quantify impact on the auth side.
Direct certificate inspection (e.g., openssl) not available via current tooling to confirm expiry and SANs.
log shard for az-b is unavailable; results exclude pods in az-b

actions.description: Deploy a renewed TLS certificate to auth-service and reload/restart the service.
actions.rationale: Eliminates the expired certificate causing handshake failures (addresses hypothesis h1).

actions.description: Verify edge-gateway trust store contains the new certificate/CA and, if needed, update it.
actions.rationale: Ensures gateway accepts the renewed cert; prevents continued 5xx.

actions.description: Run synthetic login and token‑refresh tests through edge-gateway to confirm error_rate returns to baseline (<0.5%).
actions.rationale: Validates end‑to‑end restoration of the session path.

actions.description: Add certificate‑expiry monitoring alerts (30‑day, 7‑day, 1‑day) for all services using mTLS.
actions.rationale: Detects upcoming expirations before they cause outages.

actions.description: Record the certificate renewal as a secret_rotation change in the change‑history system and enforce a mandatory rotation workflow.
actions.rationale: Closes gap G1 and provides audit trail for future incidents.

actions.description: Investigate why AZ‑b log shards were unavailable during the incident and remediate logging coverage.
actions.rationale: Removes gap G2 for future visibility.

open_questions: Who owns the certificate lifecycle for auth-service and why was the rotation missed?
Was the certificate stored in a secret manager that failed to rotate automatically?
Did any other internal services that call auth-service experience failures not captured in the current logs?
Why were AZ‑b log shards unavailable at the time of the incident?
